feedback:
This candidate changes three fields from iteration 3 (score 724.5, best raced so far): wheel_track 0.12 to 0.10, kp 5.0 to 4.5, and base_speed 1.1 to 1.0. Sensor geometry, weights, ki 0.02, kd 1.0, sensor_size and line_loss are unchanged. All values are inside the contract ranges. The sign convention and weights match every earlier design.

The evidence is that the oval (20/20, 2.14 s, iteration 3) and s-bend (20/20, 2.30 s) finish with time to spare, while the slalom is the bottleneck: 19 of 20 runs leave the track at mean progress 0.67 in iteration 3 and 0.63 in iteration 4. Iteration 4 showed that raising kp from 4.5 to 5.0 did not help the slalom (progress fell from 0.67 to 0.63) and raised steering_oscillation (0.33 to 0.31 slalom, 0.20 to 0.25 s-bend), so more kp alone has reached its limit. Iteration 3 showed that moving sensors forward to y 0.08 and raising kd to 1.0 both helped (625 to 724), so those stay.

The hypothesis is that yaw authority per unit of PWM difference is the limit. The contract's physics makes turn rate proportional to the wheel speed difference divided by wheel_track, so a narrower track should give more yaw per control output. Reducing kp to 4.5 keeps the oscillation risk down while that change takes effect. Lowering base_speed to 1.0 gives the slalom bends more margin. The cost is time. Scaling from iteration 3's oval (2.14 s at speed 1.1) suggests roughly 2.4 s at speed 1.0, and the s-bend roughly 2.6 s, so both should stay under 3 s.

Three fields change at once, so if the result is mixed the cause is harder to isolate. Read the race in this order: completion and progress on the oval and s-bend (is time still under 3 s?), then slalom progress and max_error (does the bend exit improve?), then steering_oscillation (is the narrower track causing jitter?). Decide next steps from those measurements. This candidate is a reasonable test of the yaw-authority hypothesis and is not obviously broken, so it should race now.
requested_changes: If the slalom still ends off_track with progress below 0.8 while the oval and s-bend still finish under 3 s, raise kd from 1.0 to 1.2 with wheel_track 0.10 and base_speed 1.0 kept. Iteration 3 showed kd 0.8 to 1.0 gave better slalom and s-bend results, and kd damps the stronger corrections a narrower track produces.

If steering_oscillation rises above about 0.4 (iteration 3 slalom 0.33, s-bend 0.20 to 0.25), set wheel_track to 0.11 as a midpoint between 0.10 and 0.12 before lowering kp further, so the yaw gain rise is moderated rather than removed.
If the oval or s-bend stops finishing, or completion_time on either exceeds 2.8 s, return base_speed to 1.1 with wheel_track 0.10 kept, because iteration 3 at speed 1.1 finished both tracks 20/20.
